parsed_action.internal_note: Participant B acknowledges the organization policy and the reimbursement mechanics. B will decide an initial claim amount without knowing B's actual receipt cost (random 2-8). B aims to maximize personal payoff: reimbursement minus own receipt cost. Since the reimbursement payment is the smaller of requested amount and the colleague's approved amount, and approvals are limited to verified receipt cost, B should claim close to an expected receipt cost to maximize reimbursement. B will also consider the public amount cap of 10. After seeing A's claim and receipt cost, B will review A's claim and approve up to A's receipt cost, balancing approval to ensure fair reimbursement to A without reducing own payoff. The strategy for B is to claim an amount near the expected receipt cost (around 5) to avoid underclaiming and to avoid excessive overclaiming that could reduce payoff. B will monitor A's claim and adjust approval accordingly.
